wiki_text: Aqaba has hosted a sequence of short-term chartered FSRUs pending completion of the permanent Sheikh Sabah LNG Terminal: (1) Golar Eskimo / Energos Eskimo, operating 2015-Jun 2025, then departed for Egypt; (2) Energos Force, arrived Jul 2025 on a sub-charter from Germany's DET, served Jordan and (via the Arab Gas Pipeline) Egypt jointly - Egypt ended its own 6-month draw on the vessel in Dec 2025; (3) Excelerate Acadia, a newbuild FSRU (1,000 MMcf/d, 170,000 cbm) originally built for Excelerate's Iraq integrated import terminal, temporarily redeployed to Jordan on a 9-month NEPCO timecharter (executed 5 May 2026) after the Iraq project slipped to 2027; Acadia arrived at Aqaba's jetty in the week before 29 Jun 2026 and was in commissioning as of that date, with Force still moored alongside pending its own redeployment to Germany's Stade LNG terminal (ops there targeted Sept 2026). This interim-FSRU model is expected to end once the permanent onshore ORU + BW LNG-chartered FSU (Sheikh Sabah LNG Terminal, T100001048176) enters service, targeted Q3-Q4 2026 / Sept 2026.

topic: Permanent FSU charter (BW LNG) - vessel not yet named
wiki_text: NEPCO signed a 10-year charter with BW LNG (BW Energy) in Sept 2024 for a floating storage unit (FSU) to be moored at the Sheikh Sabah LNG Terminal from Q3-Q4 2026; NEPCO takes ownership of the converted LNG carrier at the end of the 10-year term. As of the charter announcement, the specific vessel had not been named - the Riviera/BW LNG source speculated it was unlikely to be one of the two ex-Stena Bulk tri-fuel carriers (BW Enn Crystal Sky / BW Clear Sky, both already chartered elsewhere) and more plausibly the 2006-built Blue Dragon 1 (ex-Stena Blue Sky), though this was not confirmed.
